articles.title: Sebastian Stan knows 'Fjord' is 'divisive.' He wants to talk about it.
articles.summary: Sebastian Stan has seen your "knee-jerk reactions" to "Fjord," about a conservative family under fire. The response is "unfortunately predictable."
articles.body:
Sebastian Stan knows 'Fjord' is 'divisive.' He wants to talk about it.

NEW YORK – Sebastian Stan knows his latest movie is bound to strike a nerve. He likes it that way.

"I'm proud when I'm a part of something that speaks to a timely issue," says " The Apprentice " star, who is following up his Oscar-nominated role as a young Donald Trump with an equally provocative new drama.

Loosely inspired by a true story, " Fjord " (in select theaters Oct. 9, expanding nationwide Oct. 23) follows a devoutly Christian family led by stern Romanian patriarch Mihai (Stan) and his Norwegian wife, Lisbet ( Renate Reinsve ), who works in a nursing home.

When they relocate to Lisbet's hometown, the conservative clan instantly raises eyebrows among their progressive new neighbors – specifically, when the children's teachers discover bruises on their bodies and the kids confess there's occasional physical discipline at home. They are soon taken away by child protective services, sparking a prolonged legal battle.

"Fjord" grapples with cultural clashes and individual freedom, asking at what point it is our responsibility to police others' values and behavior. The Oscar hopeful won Cannes Film Festival's top prize , the Palme d'Or, in May. But it has also sparked debate among critics and social media users , some of whom believe that it props up right-wing ideology with the film's depiction of protesters rushing to Mihai and Lisbet's defense, claiming religious persecution.

"They're not understanding the nuances," says Stan, 44, on a recent visit to USA TODAY's studio. "I find it almost laughable to label it a 'MAGA film' when it's essentially about an immigrant family going to a different country and being torn apart. We could change Norway for the United States, and Romania for Mexico, or any number of places where that's happening."

Despite "these knee-jerk reactions," it's a film "that has to be processed and downloaded," Stan adds. "In America, it's going right to the heart of this divisive issue that we're currently having, and the reason people are writing it off or feel it's a propaganda piece is because we've normalized finger-pointing. This judgmental, dismissive attitude that plays out online is quite dangerous and naïve – but it's unfortunately predictable in today's time."

As a Romanian immigrant, 'Fjord' felt like 'a coming home' for Sebastian Stan

Born in Romania, Stan and his mother moved to Austria when he was 8 after the Romanian Revolution. They eventually settled in upstate New York when he was 12.

Although his family wasn't particularly religious, "I still had exposure to emotionally guarded, stoic, Eastern European male figures," he recalls. As an immigrant, he understood what it means to "feel different, have an accent, try to make new friends, and have that self-awareness that inevitably ends up carrying a slight degree of shame with it."

After working in the U.S. for roughly two decades, "Fjord" felt like "a bit of a coming-home party for me," Stan says. It's written and directed by Romanian filmmaker Cristian Mungiu, and it's the actor's first movie in which he gets to substantially speak his native language.

"I felt very embraced by the Romanian crew," he recalls. "I hung out with them every night; we spoke Romanian every day. Because I left [the country] so early, I felt like I'd been playing catch-up for a very long time. I definitely feel like I've arrived back to some old place that I left."

Scarlett Johansson, Pedro Pascal arrive at New York Film Festival 2026

In making "Fjord," Stan was very intrigued by the prospect of going to "morally ambiguous" places. While prepping for the project, he had extensive conversations with Mungiu and Reinsve about the characters' respective childhoods. They also visited churches and spoke to parents who have been embroiled in similar legal cases.

"This movie deals a lot with history and tradition, and whether it still has value in today's world. And if so, what still works and what doesn't?" Stan says. "In terms of my own upbringing culturally, there was a sense of: Stick to your own lane, stay suspicious and stay guarded. Also, if you got in trouble, you really got in trouble – and maybe that did involve spanking or a slap here and there.

"I was a very accident-prone kid and I scared my mom," he adds. "I could see she had the right intentions to protect me."

Sebastian Stan says the movie is 'very relevant for me' as a new dad

Stan and his partner, actress Annabelle Wallis, welcomed their first child in July. As a result, "this idea of what we are passing onto our kids is very relevant for me at this time in my life," he says. "It's a movie about: How do you raise kids in today's world? I've been thinking a lot about the things I learned that I'm inevitably passing down."

The Golden Globe winner admittedly has "many" fears about raising a kid in 2026.

"All you have to do is just look at the news, and how we're treating our planet and ourselves," Stan says. "But on a personal level, you always have to look at what you have control over. Even though, as a parent, I have the best intentions for my kid, it doesn't necessarily mean that I am somehow free of fault or making a mistake. It's very easy to impose your own perspective, and not see your child for who she or he or they may naturally exist to be.

"Suppression is a major issue," he adds. "Any time something is suppressed or denied, it grows another head in some capacity."

Since 2011, Stan has been in nearly a dozen Marvel projects as Bucky Barnes, aka the Winter Soldier, and he will appear in an undisclosed role in Matt Reeves' upcoming " The Batman: Part II ." But he has also stretched himself in audacious independent fare including " A Different Man ," "Fresh" and "I, Tonya."

"I like Sebastian when he has to play something very different to what he does in the Marvel movies," says Mungiu, praising the mix of menace and warmth that Stan brings to Mihai. "He is very versatile and capable of expressing a lot by doing very little."

Stan fell in love with acting in high school, and "I never thought I was going to end up in this one role that I was going to be defined by," he says. "I'm always indebted to Marvel because it opened these doors, but I feel like I'm getting to do now what I always wanted to do when I was younger. We're all so overexposed now that it's easy to get comfortable – and I worry about getting too comfortable."

articles.title: Escola Almirante Soares Dutra vence o Festival de Bandas de Santarém 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Banda Musical da escola conquistou o primeiro lugar com 318,7 pontos; na categoria Infantojuvenil, a campeã foi a Escola Municipal Maria da Conceição Figueira.
articles.summary: Banda Musical da escola conquistou o primeiro lugar com 318,7 pontos; na categoria Infantojuvenil, a campeã foi a Escola Municipal Maria da Conceição Figueira.
articles.body:
Estudantes realizam apresentação com instrumentos de percussão durante o Festival de Bandas de Santarém na Esplanada Tapajós — Foto: Reprodução/TV Tapajós

A Escola Estadual Almirante Soares Dutra conquistou o título de campeã na categoria Banda Musical do Festival de Bandas de Santarém 2026. O resultado foi divulgado na tarde deste sábado (10), após a apuração oficial das notas, em Santarém, no oeste do Pará. A escola somou 318,7 pontos e ficou à frente das outras concorrentes em uma disputa definida pela avaliação dos jurados.

A apresentação da Almirante Soares Dutra homenageou o maestro Júlio Heleno, reconhecido pelo trabalho no ensino musical de jovens estudantes da região.

O segundo lugar ficou com o Ponto de Cultura Coletivo Banda Musical Frei Ambrósio, que alcançou 316,8 pontos. A Escola Estadual Álvaro Adolfo da Silveira completou o pódio, com 316,2 pontos.

Escola municipal vence na categoria Infantojuvenil

Na categoria Banda de Percussão Infantojuvenil, a campeã foi a Escola Municipal Maria da Conceição Figueira, que obteve 256,2 pontos.

A Escola Municipal Princesa Izabel ficou em segundo lugar, com 251,6 pontos. Já o Centro de Artes Professora Josefa Borges, de Belterra, conquistou a terceira colocação, com 250,4 pontos.

As escolas classificadas em primeiro, segundo e terceiro lugares nas categorias premiadas dividiram R$ 150 mil em premiações, conforme a organização do festival.

O resultado consolidado e as notas atribuídas pelos jurados em cada quesito estão disponíveis no canal oficial da Prefeitura de Santarém no YouTube.

articles.title: Olivia Culpo and Christian McCaffrey Welcome 2nd Baby, a Boy: ‘Heart Is Exploding’
articles.summary: The couple, who wed in 2024, are also parents to 14-month-old daughter Colette
articles.body:
Olivia Culpo and Christian McCaffrey have welcomed their second baby, a boy

The couple announced on Instagram on Oct. 10 that their son, Roman Augustus, was born on Sept. 29

Culpo and McCaffrey, who wed in 2024, are also parents to 14-month-old daughter Colette

The model, 34, and her husband, Christian McCaffrey , announced in a joint Instagram post shared on Saturday, Oct. 10, that they welcomed their second baby, a boy, on Sept. 29.

"Roman Augustus McCaffrey 🤍," Culpo captioned the post, revealing her newborn's name alongside black-and-white photos of herself in the hospital as she gave birth with her NFL star husband, 30, by her side.

In the photos, the couple, who wed in 2024, could be seen holding their son at the hospital as their 14-month-old daughter, Colette , looked on. Another shot showed Culpo standing in a garden as she held Roman and Colette stood by her side.

"Heart is exploding," the proud mom added in an Instagram Stories post.

Culpo and McCaffrey first announced the news of her second pregnancy on Culpo's 34th birthday in May.

"Best birthday gift ❤️ Baby #2 coming soon 🥹," Culpo captioned a joint Instagram post, which included photos of the pair on a picnic with Colette and their dog, Oliver. A strip of sonogram images was displayed on their picnic blanket.

Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.

They later posted a video showing the moment they found out Culpo was pregnant — and how they told their families the happy news.

At the beginning of the video, Culpo and McCaffrey were seen waiting for the results of a pregnancy test.

"You're pregnant!" the San Francisco 49ers running back said before the video cut to them telling their family.

The couple announced their daughter Colette's birth in a joint July 2025 Instagram post , featuring black-and-white photos of themselves with the baby moments after she was born. Shortly after, Culpo shared several color photos from the day on her Instagram Stories as she described childbirth as "the scariest and most rewarding of all experiences."

Last October, Culpo opened up about life at home with her daughter. The new mom shared that she was initially worried that becoming a mom would impact her career.

"There's totally a shift," she said of motherhood during an episode of The Squeeze podcast. "Whether or not you want there to be or not, you have somebody that's physically dependent on you. So I'm not going to sugarcoat it. Yeah, it's scary."

However, Culpo explained that she's been able to lean on her NFL player husband while she's navigated finding a balance between working and motherhood.

"I'm so grateful that I have my husband because while I'm totally working and I'm doing everything in my power to keep working and I'm so happy to have the opportunities that I have," she explained. "Let's say they all went away — would I have the same ability 10, 12, 15, 20 years ago to light that fire up my butt when I have somebody who really needs me, which is my baby? No."

"And I would choose my baby 10 times over, obviously," she added.

articles.title: Tom Zé chega hoje aos 90 anos como o tropicalista desgarrado e inquieto que sempre confunde para explicar | G1
articles.body:
Tom Zé faz 90 anos hoje, domingo, 11 de outubro — Foto: Fernando Laszlo / Divulgação

♬ “Eu tô te explicando / Pra te confundir / Eu tô te confundindo / Pra te esclarecer”, jogou com as palavras Tom Zé em versos do samba “Tô” (1976), composto em parceria com Elton Medeiros (1930 – 2019 )e lançado por Tom há 50 anos no álbum “Estudando o samba” (1976).

Esses versos traduzem o espírito inquieto de Tom Zé e, não por acaso, eles foram apresentados em um dos títulos mais importantes e vanguardistas da discografia deste baiano de Irará (BA) nascido Antônio José Santana Martins em 11 de outubro de 1936, há exatos 90 anos.

Sim, Tom Zé cruza hoje a barreira dos 90 anos como o tropicalista resistente, desgarrado e travesso que sempre confundiu para explicar o que significa de fato ser tropicalista.

Com a alma de um erê , o artista sempre foi uma espécie de Chacrinha (1917 – 1988), o apresentador de TV cujo bordão “Eu vim para confundir e não para explicar” já teve a autoria reivindicada por Tom Zé.

Tom Zé chega aos 90 anos em atividade. Na sexta-feira, 9 de outubro, fez um show comemorativo da efeméride no Circo Voador (RJ), palco de resistência da cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ). E vem desenvolvendo um projeto musical para dar continuidade à obra singular e inclassificável que constrói desde a década de 1960.

A trajetória de Tom Zé inclui conexões importantes com os grupos Os Mutantes e Novos Baianos. A ligação com Os Mutantes é notória, até porque Tom Zé é parceiro de Rita Lee (1947 – 2023) em “2001” (1968) – uma das músicas mais famosas do grupo – e em “Qualquer bobagem” (1969), esta também assinada por Arnaldo Baptista e Sérgio Dias.

Já a relação com os Novos Baianos é menos conhecida. Mas o fato é que foi Tom Zé quem, em 1967, apresentou Moraes Moreira (1947 – 2020) – para quem dava aulas de violão – ao poeta Luiz Galvão (1937 – 2022), se tornando o mentor da parceria fundamental que gerou o grupo em 1969, ano em que Tom Zé defendeu a canção “Jeitinho dela” (Tom Zé) com os Novos Baianos no V Festival da Música Popular Brasileira.

Quando ainda estava em Salvador (BA), a trajetória de Tom Zé se entrelaça com as de Caetano Veloso, Gal Costa (1945 – 2022), Gilberto Gil e Maria Bethânia – com os quais fez o histórico show “Nós, por exemplo” em 1964.

Tom Zé é do rebanho tropicalista. Mas logo deixou evidente que seria a ovelha desgarrada. É que Tom Zé nunca fez música para gerar mero sucesso comercial, nunca fez o jogo da indústria. Os jogos armados pelo cantor e compositor no palco ou no estúdio sempre foram puramente estéticos. Tom Zé é e sempre foi um erê que se recusa a entrar na roda-viva do mundo dos adultos sedentos de glória, poder, dinheiro e fama.

Na trajetória mercadologicamente errática, Tom Zé amargou o fracasso comercial de álbuns que somente seriam valorizados anos depois, sobretudo após David Byrne se deparar casualmente em 1986 com o já mencionado álbum “Estudando o samba” e se encantar com a inventividade do disco, compilando a obra de Tom Zé para CD do selo Luaka Bop e, na sequência, lançando pelo selo álbuns inéditos do artista, como “The hips of tradition” (1991) – o que deu prestígio e visibilidade mundial ao último romântico tropicalista.

O encontro de Byrne com Tom Zé em 1988, na cidade de São Paulo (SP), mudou a vida do artista baiano após anos de ostracismo e desânimos com a dificuldade de se fazer ouvir – o que fez Tom Zé cogitar a desistir da carreira e a voltar para a cidade natal de Irará (BA).

Tom Zé, contudo, perseverou e continuou em cena, recebendo as flores em vida. Álbuns gravados após a redescoberta – casos de “Com defeito da fabricação” (1998), “Jogos de armar (Faça você mesmo)” (2000), “Estudando o pagode” (2005), “Estudando a bossa” (2008) e “Tropicália lixo lógico” (2012) – dialogaram com títulos mais antigos como “Tom Zé” (1968), “Tom Zé” (1970), “Tom Zé” (1972), “Todos os olhos” (1973) e “Correio da Estação do Brás” (1978), encorpando discografia pautada pela coerência e pela determinação de inventar.

Aos 90 anos, Tom Zé segue confundindo, mas já não precisa explicar mais nada. Tom Zé é Tom Zé. E isso é tudo. E tudo já está esclarecido.

"It’s hot in LA," Klum captioned the post, which shows her lounging topless on a daybed with her dog, with a large grass field and a swimming pool visible behind her. articles.title: When Amitabh Bachchan recalled his first film salary, he said: 'I felt I should give it to my parents'
articles.summary: Amitabh Bachchan once revealed that his immediate thought after securing his debut film was to give his earnings to his parents.
articles.body: Amitabh Bachchan once revealed that his immediate thought after securing his debut film was to give his earnings to his parents. During a 2023 episode of 'Kaun Banega Crorepati 15', he spoke about how the opportunity gave him a chance to take care of his parents, Harivansh Rai Bachchan and Teji Bachchan.The conversation took place when contestant Vivek asked Amitabh Bachchan about his first film. Recalling his experience with 'Saat Hindustani', the actor explained that he wanted to use his earnings to bring his parents to live with him. He also spoke about assuming the responsibilities they had carried while raising him.“Humko ye laga ki isase hume jo bhi milega, wo hum apne ma-babuji ko de dein. Mujhe ek zariya mil gaya ki apne ma-babuji ko bula kar apne paas rakhein. Jo zimmedari unhone humare liye jeevan bhar kiya hai us zimmedari ko hum apne kandho par rakh kar aage unke liye kar ke dein.”(“I felt that whatever I earned from this, I should give it to my parents. I had found a way to bring them to live with me. They had taken care of us and fulfilled their responsibilities throughout their lives. I wanted to take those responsibilities onto my own shoulders and take care of them from then on.”)Amitabh Bachchan’s first film and his parentsFor Amitabh Bachchan, the opportunity to act in 'Saat Hindustani' also represented a way to become financially independent and support his family. Rather than focusing only on the prospects of a film career, he remembered thinking about how his first earnings could help his parents.Before entering films, Amitabh Bachchan had been looking for employment in Kolkata. His path towards acting changed after his friend Tinnu Anand recommended him to filmmaker Khwaja Ahmad Abbas. Abbas was looking for new faces for his film 'Saat Hindustani'. According to a 2021 Hindustan Times report, the filmmaker spoke to Harivansh Rai Bachchan before finalising the actor. Khwaja Ahmad Abbas wanted to ensure that Amitabh Bachchan’s father supported his son’s decision to pursue acting.What 'Saat Hindustani' was aboutReleased in 1969, 'Saat Hindustani' followed seven Indian revolutionaries who challenged Portuguese rule in Goa. Amitabh Bachchan portrayed a poet in the film, which marked his debut on the big screen. The project became an important starting point for the actor, who would go on to build a career spanning several decades. His early performance also earned him his first National Film Award in the Most Promising Newcomer category.Over the years, Amitabh Bachchan has continued to work in cinema while maintaining a strong presence on television through 'Kaun Banega Crorepati'. articles.title: Chiranjeevi calls Amitabh Bachchan ‘Guru Ji’ wishing him on 84th birthday; write ‘Your love for cinema has always been an inspiration’
articles.summary: Megastar Chiranjeevi shared his birthday wishes to Bollywood legend Amitabh Bachchan as he turned 84 on Sunday.
articles.body: Megastar Chiranjeevi shared his birthday wishes to Bollywood legend Amitabh Bachchan as he turned 84 on Sunday. Calling him his “dearest Guru Ji,” the Telugu veteran praised Bachchan’s love for cinema, dedication to his craft and inspiring personality.Taking to social media, Chiranjeevi shared a heartfelt note celebrating the veteran actor’s achievements and the respect he continues to command in the film industry.Chiranjeevi wishes Amitabh Bachchan on his birthday“Happy Birthday to my dearest Guru Ji @SrBachchan. Your love for cinema and the respect you bring to your craft have always been an inspiration to me,” Chiranjeevi wrote.Chiranjeevi praises Bachchan’s humilityChiranjeevi also mentioned Amitabh Bachchan’s warmth and humility, saying these qualities make him special beyond his professional achievements.“Beyond your towering achievements, it is your warmth and humility that make you so special. Wishing you good health, endless happiness and many more memorable years doing what you love. With all my love and respect, Sir!” he added.The post featured a picture of the two veteran actors sharing a warm hug.Amitabh Bachchan celebrated his 84th birthday on October 11. Several members of the film industry and fans took to social media to wish Big B.Today, the Shahenshah of Bollywood took to his X handle to write, “T 5882 - Morning has arrived, and here I am, sitting with you!”Amitabh Bachchan’s outing with Chiranjeevi in ‘Sye Raa Narasimha Reddy’The two actors worked together in the historical action film ‘Sye Raa Narasimha Reddy’ making a special appearance. In 2019, Chiranjeevi approached Amitabh Bachchan to play Gosayi Venkanna, the guru of his character in the film. Chiranjeevi reportedly sought Jaya Bachchan’s help to convey the request, as he was hesitant to approach the Bollywood megastar directly.Amitabh Bachchan agreed to the role without hesitation. He reportedly declined remuneration for his appearance and also turned down the offer of a private jet, making his own travel and accommodation arrangements.In 2024, Amitabh Bachchan was last seen in ‘Vettaiyan’ alongside Rajinikanth and played Ashwatthama in Nag Ashwin’s mythological sci-fi ‘Kalki 2898 AD’. He will also be seen in the second part of the film.Meanwhile, Chiranjeevi is shooting for his next project ‘Kaaka’ helmed by Bobby Kolli. articles.title: Exclusive! Navratri special: Vaani Kapoor: The beauty of Navratri is that we honour the feminine in many forms’
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview, actress Vaani Kapoor reflects on the significance of Navratri, sharing childhood memories and emphasizing the importance of women's empowerment beyond celebrations. Discover her thoughts on the vibrance of Navratri in Mumbai versus Delhi and the importance of connecting across generations.
articles.body: For Vaani Kapoor, Navratri is a celebration of tradition, family and the many facets of feminine strength. Having grown up in Delhi and spent a significant part of her life in Mumbai, the actor has experienced the festival in different ways. In an interaction with Bombay Times, Vaani reflects on her childhood memories of Navratri, the festival’s significance and why women empowerment must go beyond symbolic celebrations.‘Festivals have a lovely way of taking you back to being a child’Talking about her fond memories of the festival, the War actress says, “Growing up in Delhi, I think what I remember most is the vibe during this time of the year. The markets would be buzzing; there’d be Ramleelas happening, and you could feel the excitement building up to Dussehra. At home, I remember the ashtami celebrations, the halwa, puri, and chana, and all the little girls who’d come over for kanjak. As kids, we were more excited about the food and all the festivities than anything else. I think festivals have a lovely way of taking you back to being a child.”‘Mumbai has introduced me to an exuberant side of Navratri’Having experienced Navratri in two cities, Vaani believes each has its own charm. “In Delhi, at least growing up, I remember Navratri being more about the family rituals, the Ramleelas, and the excitement around Dussehra. Mumbai has this wonderful energy during Navratri, with garba, dandiya, music, and everyone coming together to celebrate. Delhi will always feel nostalgic to me because it’s home, whereas Mumbai has introduced me to a different, more exuberant side of Navratri,” she says.‘Empowerment is about the freedom to make your own choices’Navratri is a celebration of the feminine energy in the universe. For Vaani, the festival’s celebration of feminine strength also offers an opportunity to reflect on how women are treated beyond the festivities. “It’s beautiful that we celebrate goddesses and the different forms of feminine strength. But I also feel there’s a difference between celebrating women and truly valuing them in everyday life. So many women grow up being told to adjust, to compromise, to put everyone else’s needs before their own. And we often praise them for how much they can endure, without asking why they should have to endure so much in the first place. Their dreams, happiness, and their individuality matter just as much,” she says.She adds, “I believe that empowerment is about the freedom to make your own choices, to feel safe, to be financially independent, to pursue your ambitions, and to have a say in decisions that affect your own life. These are things every woman deserves, regardless of her background or circumstances. And I think real progress is when women no longer have to fight for things that should be theirs to begin with.”‘There’s something particularly special about seeing women across generations celebrating together’Beyond rituals, music and dressing up, the actress believes festivals create opportunities for women to connect and celebrate themselves. “Festivals have this lovely way of bringing people together, regardless of age or background. And there’s something particularly special about seeing women across generations celebrating together during Navratri, each bringing their own energy to the festivities. So much of our everyday lives revolves around responsibilities that we sometimes forget the importance of just having fun. And I think those moments when you feel part of something where you can simply enjoy yourself, can do more for your confidence than we realise,” she says, adding, “There’s something really comforting about coming together for traditions you’ve grown up with and the memories they bring back. And what I find beautiful about Navratri is that we honour the feminine in so many forms.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: AS Roma XI vs Como – Predicted lineup and team news
articles.summary: AS Roma head to Como on Sunday aiming to reclaim outright first place in Serie A from Inter Milan.Under Gian Piero Gasperini, Roma have made a strong start t...
articles.body:
AS Roma head to Como on Sunday aiming to reclaim outright first place in Serie A from Inter Milan.

Under Gian Piero Gasperini, Roma have made a strong start to their league campaign. They sit at the top of the table with 13 points and are yet to lose in Serie A, combining an attacking return of 14 goals with just three at the other end. Their recent run included four straight victories—4-0 over Fiorentina, 4-0 against Lecce, 2-1 versus Atalanta, and 2-0 away to Torino—before they were held to a competitive 2-2 draw by fellow title contenders Inter Milan.

Roma arrive with several fitness problems following the international break. First-choice goalkeeper Mile Svilar will miss at least a month after suffering a stress fracture in his finger, meaning Pierluigi Gollini is set to deputise in goal.

The midfield is also affected, with Bryan Cristante unavailable because of knee inflammation. That could open the door for Marten de Roon to make his first start, likely alongside Manu Koné.

At the back, Konstantinos Koulierakis is still sidelined, although Evan Ndicka is available and expected to play a key role in the back three.

There is better news in attack, where in-form forward Donyell Malen has recovered from a small knock and should lead the line. Wing-back Wesley França has also been given the all-clear to feature.

However, Gasperini may choose to leave Argentine pair Leonardo Balerdi and Matías Soulé on the substitutes' bench, with their recent international travel likely to be a factor in his selection plans.

Possible AS Roma starting XI: Gollini; Mancini, Ndicka, Hermoso; Molina, Kone, De Roon, Wesley; Dybala, Mora; Malen

The match will kick off at 11:30am BST on Sunday, 10th October.

Supporters in the UK can follow the match live on DAZN, with coverage of the Serie A fixture from the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia.

articles.title: Big B’s b’day: KMC invites its star alumnus back
articles.summary: Big B’s b’day: KMC invites its star alumnus back One may wonder what makes Kirori Mal College’s auditorium so special, but for The Players, KMC’s theatre
articles.body: Big B’s b’day: KMC invites its star alumnus backOne may wonder what makes Kirori Mal College’s auditorium so special, but for The Players, KMC’s theatre society, and MUSOC, its music society, it is a place where generations of students learnt about themselves and the world. For some, the auditorium was the college itself. So, when it was left in a dilapidated state for years, the college administration, with the help of its alumni, joined forces to save their home. After multiple meetings and sustained efforts involving celebrated alumni including Amitabh Bachchan, Ali Abbas Zafar, Satish Kaushik, Raj Shekhar, Sargun Mehta, Siddharth, Divyendu, Zeeshan Ayyub and Anant Vidhaat, the auditorium is finally back in shape – ready to be reopened soon.A few days before Amitabh Bachchan’s birthday, a delegation led by Principal Dinesh Khattar met the actor on the sets of Kaun Banega Crorepati. And since no meeting with a KMC alumni is complete without a mention of the auditorium, the meeting saw the principal invite Bachchan to the college next year for the inauguration.‘Mr Bachchan’s support in renovating this auditorium has been immense’Bachchan fondly recalled his KMC days and Frank Thakurdas, the mentor who shaped his early acting career and gives the renovated auditorium its name.During the interaction, the principal formally invited Big B to inaugurate the renovated Frank Thakurdas Memorial Auditorium. “He responded graciously, expressing his willingnessto attend, subject to his professional commitments,” shared Principal Dinesh Khattar with us. “For us, it was a special occasion and from the KM staff and college, we would like to congratulate Mr Bachchan on his birthday today. His support in renovating this auditorium has been immense. For me personally, the reopening of the auditorium will represent not simply the completion of an infrastructure project, but the fulfillment of a cherished dream. Buildings acquire meaning through the lives that unfold within them, and I look forward to seeing the Frank Thakurdas Memorial Auditorium become, once again, the beating heart of Kirori Mal College,” he added.‘The auditorium has been a site of play, work and an exposure to the world’One person who has witnessed the auditorium’s fall, its difficult years and now its revival is Keval Arora. As the former staff advisor of The Players, he remembers how on issue led to another, keeping the auditorium out of use for years. “For generations of members of The Players, and I am no exception, the auditorium has been home. It is a site of playand work, with others and by oneself, an exposure to the world, its people, systems and values, a place of refuge. We are very thankful to our Principal Dinesh Khattar for his unwavering commitment and sustained efforts towards realising this dream,” he told us.Shalini Baxi, Convenor, Culture Council, KMC, and an alumna of the college’s music society, adds, “For me, the occasion was especially meaningful. It was a celebration not merely of a distinguished alumnus, but of the extraordinary cultural legacy of KMC.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Rajinikanth’s 230 avatars feature in special Navratri Kolu at Azhagumigu Sri Rajini temple ahead of 'Jailer 2' release
articles.summary: A superstar’s legacy can inspire celebrations that go far beyond cinema, and Rajinikanth’s devoted fans continue to find unique ways to express their
articles.body: A superstar’s legacy can inspire celebrations that go far beyond cinema, and Rajinikanth’s devoted fans continue to find unique ways to express their admiration. A special kolu in the Azhagumigu Sri Rajini Temple ahead of Navratri is a tribute to the actor’s incredible journey in Indian cinema. The wide-ranging exhibition includes 230-plus photos and representations of the superstar, highlighting his indelible characters and decades-long career. The annual collaboration proves that Rajinikanth’s popularity is not confined to the cinema halls, turning a customary festival display into a homage to his eternal charm.From 'Apoorva Raagangal' to 'Jailer 2': Rajinikanth fan Karthik creates 230 representationsThe special Navratri kolu, created by Karthik, traces Rajinikanth’s journey from his debut film, Apoorva Raagangal, to his upcoming projects, including 'Jailer 2' and 'Dharman.' According to ANI, Karthik began this tradition three years ago and has continued to expand the display every year. One of this year’s major attractions is a portrait of Rajinikanth drawn on a leaf. Speaking about his devotion, Karthik said he had been a fan of the actor for nearly 40 to 50 years and had collected photographs from the early days of his film career. He described Rajinikanth as his family’s kula deivam (clan deity), explaining that the annual arrangement was a personal expression of their faith and admiration.Special Rajinikanth temple Kolu features handmade portraits and daily pujasCreating the display involves more than collecting photographs. Karthik explained that the pictures are carefully cut out, mounted on foam sheets and fabric, and arranged in different styles to give each year’s kolu a distinctive appearance. The temple also conducts regular pujas, while prasadam is distributed to devotees. Different offerings, including sundal, are prepared each day during the celebrations. The temple attracts several visitors, particularly on Sundays, with many devotees sharing the family’s deep reverence for the actor. The display therefore brings together Navratri traditions, creative work and the strong emotional connection Rajinikanth has built with generations of admirers.Rajinikanth prepares for 'Jailer 2' release on October 15, 2026Meanwhile, Rajinikanth is gearing up for the release of 'Jailer 2,' directed by Nelson Dilipkumar. Scheduled to arrive in theatres on October 15, 2026, the film will see him return as Muthuvel Pandian. Its recently released trailer offers a glimpse of the character’s quieter life before events connected to his past draw him back into violence. The makers have also released the second single, 'One Sun, One Moon,' composed and sung by Anirudh Ravichander, with additional vocals by MS Krsna and lyrics by Heisenberg and Super Subu. The song celebrates Rajinikanth’s commanding screen presence and lasting appeal. The special Navratri kolu is yet another reminder of the love the superstar continues to receive from his fans as anticipation for the sequel builds.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Exclusive! Ranbir Kapoor: When your day involves a lot of people and a lot of noise, a few minutes alone can feel valuable
articles.summary: Ranbir Kapoor shares insights on the importance of solitude in a busy life, discussing his personal care brand Flux Theory and the transformative power of small rituals like taking a shower.
articles.body: Ranbir Kapoor has played characters who wear their hearts on their sleeves, run away from the ordinary and struggle to make sense of the world around them. From the brooding Jordan in Rockstar to the free-spirited Bunny in Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani, the actor has repeatedly slipped into the skin of men who are constantly negotiating with different sides of themselves. Off screen, however, life comes with its own set of demands — long shooting schedules, the pressure of getting a performance right and the responsibilities that come with being a husband and a father.In the middle of all this, finding a moment to oneself can be a luxury. For Ranbir, it need not involve an elaborate routine or a grand escape. Sometimes, it is as simple as taking a shower without having to rush through it. “After a long shoot, I like having a few minutes when nobody needs anything from me. I’m not particular about making it a ritual, but I enjoy a good fragrance and a little quiet. It helps me leave the workday behind,” he tells us.The appeal, he explains, is less about emerging from the bathroom with a sudden epiphany and more about having the space to slow down. When the day involves being surrounded by people, conversations and constant activity, a few minutes of solitude can offer a welcome breather.“When your day involves a lot of people and a lot of noise, a few minutes alone can feel valuable. I don’t come out of every shower with a big realisation. Usually, it’s much simpler than that: I’ve had a moment to slow down, and I’m ready to give my attention to whatever comes next,” he says.While Ranbir doesn't recall a specific instance of a shower helping him crack a difficult scene, he believes that taking a break from work can help him return to it with a fresh perspective. “I can’t think of a particular scene that I solved by taking a shower! But I do think it helps to get a little distance from the work when you’ve been at it for hours. A short break can clear your head, and sometimes you return to a scene with a different perspective,” he says.It is also an idea that connects with his latest entrepreneurial venture, Flux Theory, a personal-care brand he has co-founded. While the brand's premise revolves around the different versions of ourselves that emerge in different situations, Ranbir says the thinking behind it was to make an everyday activity feel more personal. “I think it’s one of the biggest yet one of the most boring categories. Personal care and shower specifically has been largely about functional products. We really wanted to make it a personal and engaging moment for everyone. Also, the idea behind Flux Theory was really interesting — it’s the belief that you get to play different versions of you. Something which I have done quite a lot in my acting career,” he says.The brand's five archetypes — Sage, Sport, Lover, Dreamer and Rebel — might seem like an extension of the many personalities an actor gets to explore on screen. Can a small everyday ritual influence which version of oneself comes to the fore? Ranbir thinks it can, albeit in a more understated way. “Small rituals can definitely affect how you feel. I wouldn’t say a shower turns you into a completely different person, but it can give you a pause between one part of your day and the next. Sometimes that little shift is enough,” he says.A cold shower, particularly after a long day, gets his vote, while music is unlikely to make it to his bathroom routine. “Usually silence. That’s my quiet time,” he says. And perhaps that is the point. In a life where he is constantly switching between film sets, public appearances and family time, those few minutes offer him something uncomplicated: a chance to switch off before stepping back into the world.Rapid Fire: Ranbir in the Bathroom1. Hot shower or cold shower?Cold shower, especially after a long day.2. Singing in the shower or complete silence?Usually silence. That’s my quiet time.3. One song that deserves to be on your shower playlist?Nowadays Barbad from Saiyaara4. If you could step out of the shower as any one of your iconic film characters, who would it be?Jordan from Rockstar. He’d make a much more dramatic entrance than I would.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Jessica Springsteen and Nicola Philippaerts share exciting family news as they prepare for their first baby
articles.summary: Bruce Springsteen’s daughter Jessica Springsteen is preparing for a major new chapter in her life.
articles.body: Bruce Springsteen’s daughter Jessica Springsteen is preparing for a major new chapter in her life. The Olympic silver medallist and her partner, Belgian show jumper Nicola Philippaerts, are expecting their first child together. The couple shared the news through a joint social media post, offering fans a glimpse of their celebration away from the equestrian arena.According to PEOPLE’s report on October 10, 2026, Jessica, 34 and Nicola, 33, posted a series of photographs from what appeared to be a Mediterranean holiday. In several pictures, Jessica can be seen gently holding a baby bump. They kept the announcement short and sweet, captioning the post, “New adventures.”Bruce Springsteen’s family is growingJessica is the only daughter of Bruce and Patti, who also have two sons, Evan and Samuel. The couple have generally kept their children’s lives away from the spotlight, even as Bruce built a decades-long career as one of rock music’s biggest names.The baby will be the family’s second grandchild. Jessica’s younger brother Samuel welcomed a daughter, Lily, in 2022.Bruce has previously spoken about watching his son become a father. During a June 2025 appearance on Michelle Obama’s IMO podcast, he reflected on Samuel’s relationship with his daughter, saying, “I watch my youngest son with his daughter, [and] he’s a better dad than I was — already.” He continued, “That gives me great pride. I go, ‘Well, he’s really doing it right, you know.’”His remarks offered a rare glimpse into the musician’s experience of family life beyond the stage. Jessica’s pregnancy now brings another milestone for the Springsteen family, although Bruce and Patti have not publicly commented on the latest announcement.Who is Nicola Philippaerts?Nicola is a Belgian professional show jumper who has competed internationally from a young age. He comes from a family deeply involved in equestrian sport: his father, Ludo Philippaerts, is a former international rider, while his twin brother, Olivier Philippaerts, is also an accomplished show jumper.According to Nicola’s biography on the Global Champions website, he enjoyed success during his junior and young-rider years, including European and Youth Olympic victories, before establishing himself at senior level.Jessica shares that passion for the sport. The pair have been linked since 2024, according to Us Weekly. Although their professional lives involve frequent travel and international competitions, they have largely kept their relationship private.Jessica Springsteen’s journey to Olympic successJessica’s own achievements have brought her recognition beyond her famous family name. She represented the United States in team jumping at the Tokyo Olympics, officially known as Tokyo 2020, which took place in 2021 after the pandemic-related postponement. The U.S. team won the silver medal.Her father celebrated the achievement publicly during an episode of his SiriusXM show From My Home to Yours in August 2021. As reported by the Asbury Park Press, Bruce said, “I want to congratulate the United States Olympic show jumping team — that’s McLain Ward, Laura Kraut and my lovely daughter, Jessica Springsteen — on their silver medal win at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.”Patti Scialfa also congratulated her daughter on social media. She wrote, “BRINGING HOME THE SILVER—Congratulations to the USA 2020 Equestrian Jumping Team!! What a day…what a ride…”Jessica’s Olympic achievement was the result of years of dedication to riding, a sport she pursued long before becoming widely recognised as Bruce Springsteen’s daughter.A new adventure beyond competitionFor Jessica Springsteen and Nicola Philippaerts, the pregnancy marks a personal milestone alongside their careers in professional equestrian sport. Their announcement offered few details, but the affectionate photos and brief caption gave followers a glimpse of their excitement.As they prepare to become parents, the couple are beginning a chapter that will take them beyond the competition arena. For the Springsteen family, it is another reason to celebrate.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Pier premiere celebrates Cromer film-maker's work
articles.summary: Rupert Harold says the rags to riches film was shot across Europe and Norfolk.
articles.body:
A town has turned out in force to support a 19-year-old film-maker ahead of his new film being released on a major streaming platform.

Rupert Harold from Cromer in Norfolk has made his second feature film and has set his sights on becoming the youngest director to win an Oscar.

His film, Crecista, is a rags to riches story filmed across locations in Norfolk, Lake Como, Milan and Naples and features helicopters, sports cars and a yacht, all within a £2,000 budget. The film will be streamed on Amazon Prime.

He said: "The film was received so well I felt such an overwhelming feeling of support and just a great community feel... I don't think it could have gone better."

The red carpet was rolled out on Cromer Pier on Tuesday for a debut screening of the film ahead of its release on Saturday.

He said: "The premiere was absolutely amazing, we had about 400 people there.

"We had supercars, a Ferrari, a Porsche, Rolls Royce and a Corvette there which was crazy."

Crecista, follows a struggling British man who builds a fortune by illegally selling classified government information.

Harold said Cromer Pier features in the film as does central Norwich.

He added: "We also have Blakeney, we have some of the marshes and various shots in Sheringham and we have Sheringham Little Theatre there as well."

Despite working with a budget of just £2,000, Harold contacted people who were kind enough to let him use helicopters, fancy cars, a yacht club and hotel for filming.

Harold started film-making at eight years old and, after getting in contact with Amazon when he was 15, his first feature film Dengard was released when he was 17.

Harold said he was inspired by films including the 1990 film GoodFellas starring Robert De Niro and directed by Martin Scorsese.

He said: "Film-making is so unique because you are able to transport someone into a world you have created for that set amount of time so I'm super excited to see what people think of the story.

"My ambition has always been to win an Oscar for the youngest director. When I was 17, for my last film I stated that I'm going to win an Oscar at 27."

Off the back of filming across Europe, Harold has big plans to take his third feature film to Montana in the United States.

"We're really excited for that and kind of hoping to make a break into Hollywood from the UK and obviously from Norfolk," he said.
